sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: HEK293/HEK293T cells expressing HA-tagged full-length CL1 were incubated with neurexin-1α and -1β Ig-fusion proteins (±SS4 insert); specific binding was detected, demonstrating that the HA-tagged receptor is surface-displayed and retains neurexin-binding function. The HA tag in ECL1 did not abolish neurexin interaction.
sites.rationale: L1 names the exact junction ('between Tyr918 and Glu919 in the first extracellular loop') in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct. Python search of the canonical sequence locates the YE motif at positions 919–920 (a one-residue offset from the paper's numbering, consistent with a minor rat-vs-human or isoform difference); the junction is unambiguous because YE is the only such dinucleotide in ECL1. The insert sits 34 residues from the TM1 C-terminal boundary (885) and 4 residues from the TM2 N-terminal boundary (923), both satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance constraint. L2 and L3 confirm surface display and preserved neurexin binding, qualifying this as surface_and_function. Full-length CL1 (ADGRL1/latrophilin-1) expressed in HEK293/HEK293T cells with an HA epitope inserted by PCR 'between Tyr918 and Glu919 in the first extracellular loop of CL1' (L1, PMC3308797). The paper uses a numbering that is offset by one relative to the canonical human UniProt sequence (Q9ULB1): the YE motif in ECL1 (topology span 915–922) falls at positions 919–920 in the canonical sequence. Python search confirmed seq[918]='Y' and seq[919]='E', unambiguously locating the junction. L2 and L3 confirm that HA-tagged CL1 is displayed on the cell surface and retains the ability to bind soluble neurexin-1α and -1β fusion proteins.

sources.claim:
Only pCMVIg-CL1 Lectin that encodes CL1 residues Met 1 –Tyr 131 fused to human IgG Fc fragment was cloned by direct insertion of a PCR fragment into the EcoRI-SalI site of pCMVIg vector.
pCMV-CL1-1 and pCMV-CL1-5 encode full-length CL1 lacking both splice inserts or containing an insert in SSA, respectively (CL1 FL and CL1 FL+SSA ) and were described previously ( 6 ). pCMV-CL1 HA encodes full-length CL1 lacking both splice inserts in which the HA epitope was inserted by PCR between Tyr 918 and Glu 919 in the first extracellular loop of CL1.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display of the N-terminally FLAG-tagged full-length receptor was used in cell-based assays (PMC3321182). The independent mouse knock-in (PMC11154861) confirmed immunolocalization of the endogenous 2xmyc-tagged Lphn1 at synapses, demonstrating surface trafficking of the tagged receptor in vivo. No quantitative functional assay result is reported for the FLAG construct alone in L4.
sites.rationale: L4 explicitly states 'The Flag epitope was fused at Leu25 of CL1', and the topology landmarks place the signal peptide at residues 1–24, making Leu25 (seq[24]='L') the first residue of the mature extracellular N-terminus. The tag therefore sits after residue 24 (seq[23]='G'), well upstream of TM1 (865), with 840 residues of extracellular space between the junction and the first TM helix. L7 independently pins the identical junction in the mouse ortholog knock-in, raising confidence that this terminus tolerates an epitope tag without disrupting folding or trafficking. Full-length human CL1 (ADGRL1/latrophilin-1) expressed in cells with a FLAG epitope fused at Leu25, the first residue of the mature protein after signal-peptide cleavage (SP = residues 1–24). The same N-terminal junction is independently corroborated by a mouse knock-in line (L7, PMC11154861) in which a 2xmyc tag was inserted 'just after the signal peptide and before the lectin-like domain', confirming the junction is conserved and tolerated in the endogenous receptor.

sources.claim: The Flag epitope was fused at Leu25 of CL1.

literature_notes: Two ledger-supported sites were identified. (1) The N-terminal junction after the signal peptide (insert_after_residue=24) is pinned by L4 (FLAG at Leu25, human CL1) and independently corroborated by L5/L6/L7 (2xmyc knock-in mouse at the identical junction); because both papers pin the same junction it is reported as one site, cited to L4 as the most precise human-sequence reference. Validation is surface_only for L4 because no quantitative functional assay result is reported for that specific construct; the mouse knock-in (L7) adds immunolocalization evidence but is an ortholog. (2) The ECL1 HA-tag site (insert_after_residue=919) is the most strongly validated site: the paper names the exact flanking residues, the construct is full-length and membrane-anchored, and neurexin binding is preserved (surface_and_function). The one-residue numbering offset between the paper (Tyr918/Glu919) and the canonical human sequence (Y919/E920) was resolved by Python sequence search; the YE motif is unique in ECL1. No ledger lines describe intracellular insertions or function-abrogating insertions for ADGRL1, so other_positions is empty. L2 and L3 are corroborating lines for Site 2 (same paper, same construct) and are not cited separately as they do not add a new junction.
